title: Affine-local cohomology classes detect maps out of ordinary higher direct image
statement: Let f:X→Y be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and p∈ℕ. For each open V of Y put U=f⁻¹(V), j_U:U→X, let H_U^p be module cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology] on U, and forget its global scalar action. There are natural transformations in the coefficient O_X-module M, c_V: H_U^p(j_U^*(-))→Γ(V,R^p f_*(-)), where restriction is [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits] and ordinary module higher direct image is [pqf-def-cohomology]. For every module N on X [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], module Q on Y, and maps a,b:R^p f_*N→Q, if c_V(N) followed by Γ(V,a) equals c_V(N) followed by Γ(V,b) for every affine open V, then a=b. No compactness, quasi-separatedness, quasi-coherence, family, or coproduct hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 20.7.3; coefficient naturality of the injective-resolution comparison, using Lemma 20.7.1 (Tag 01E1)

proof.text: For each coefficient module M choose an injective resolution I. Open restriction is exact and carries I to an injective resolution on U (01E1). Through overFunctorEquiv, the resolution is a resolution of Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι applied to M. The restrictAppIso at top identifies its global sections complex with the sections of I over U; forgetting scalars is exact, so the resulting homology is the underlying additive group of H^p(U,M|U).

This section complex is also the evaluation at V of f_*I. Map its homology through sectionCohomologyTheta, then through the inverse of I.isoRightDerivedObj f_* p. This defines c_V(M). Lift every coefficient map to a map of the chosen resolutions. The restricted lift preserves the augmentation; isoRightDerivedObj_hom_naturality, naturality of mapHomologyIso, and the adjunction unit/counit identities show that the displayed maps commute with this lift. Homotopic lifts give identical homology maps, yielding a natural transformation on coefficient modules.

The comparison of the cohomology presheaf with R^p f_*N is an isomorphism on stalks. Each germ is the image of a class on a neighborhood; restrict that class to an affine sub-neighborhood using the restriction compatibility in the higher-direct-image presheaf lemma. The assumed equality of composites with c_V(N) gives equality after applying a and b to this germ. Since all germs have such representatives, a and b agree on all stalks. For a section over W, equal stalk images at every point of W imply local equality and hence equality by sheaf uniqueness, proving a=b. For empty Y there are no germs and uniqueness is vacuous; p=0 uses the same resolution maps.

proof_origin.place: Coefficient-natural form of the cohomology-presheaf description and its affine-basis detection consequence

theorem higherDirectImage_affine_cohomology_presentation
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (p : ℕ) :
    ∃ c : ∀ V : Y.Opens,
      Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι ⋙
        RingedSpace.moduleCohomology (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace p ⋙
          forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u}
            ((moduleRings (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)))
              AddCommGrpCat.{u} ⟶
      (RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage f.toLRSHom.toShHom).rightDerived p ⋙
        RingedSpace.openModuleSections Y.toRingedSpace V,
      ∀ (N : X.Modules) (Q : Y.Modules)
        (a b : ((RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage f.toLRSHom.toShHom).rightDerived p).obj N ⟶ Q),
        (∀ (V : Y.Opens), IsAffineOpen V →
          (c V).app N ≫ (RingedSpace.openModuleSections Y.toRingedSpace V).map a =
            (c V).app N ≫ (RingedSpace.openModuleSections Y.toRingedSpace V).map b) →
        a = b
